match_note: v1 (20 Jun 2025, 12 pages, main text only, no supplement) contains the text the referees quote or describe before revision: the abstract phrase 'enables advanced functional design', the JS values 'motivated by the magnitude of the induced magnetic moments in the Ta layer as calculated by density functional theory', the statement that the edge-mode maximum lies in the ML (later withdrawn), the BL morphology sentence without the clause the rebuttal says was added, no discussion of YSR or Andreev states (added in revision), and matching figure numbers (Fig. 4c spectra, Fig. 5c,d stripe geometry, Fig. 6 band structure, Supp. Figs. S16 to S18). Only difference found: Ref. 21 renders correctly in v1. Supplementary figures (S6, S7, S9) cannot be checked because v1 has no supplement. Round 3 (Version 2) has only R2, who recommends publication with no new concerns.

concerns.quote: what I find missing is the novelty from the manuscript. Although the paper is technically sound, I was not convinced that this manuscript brings significant advancement in the fundamental understanding of MSH
concerns.summary: The work lacks novelty and does not significantly advance understanding of magnet-superconductor hybrids.

concerns.quote: It is also not clear to me how the observation of these spin-polarized edge states “enables advanced functional design” ... the authors should discuss how they can be detected with other experimental methods and being used in complex circuits.
concerns.summary: The claimed application potential is unsupported; the authors should explain how these substrate-bound edge states could be detected by other methods and used in circuits.
concerns.note: Merges R1 opening paragraph and R1 point 6; the abstract and discussion of v1 contain the 'advanced functional design' claim.

concerns.quote: What is the condition to have an edge state between two topological nodal superconductors? ... any small change in the material parameters could move the position of the nodal points and hence create an edge state
concerns.summary: Without a topological invariant, it is unclear what guarantees an edge mode between two nodal-point superconductors, and if any small parameter change creates one, observing it means little.

concerns.quote: The band structure of monolayer Mn on Ta(110) in Figure 6 appears to be quite different from ... monolayer Mn on Nb(110) ... how sensitive/ robust is the topological nodal point superconductivity to material parameters?
concerns.summary: The modelled band structure differs from the same group's earlier model of a similar system, raising questions about parameter choices and robustness of the nodal-point phase.

concerns.quote: I am not entirely convinced that the experimentally observed edge state is located at the ML. ... The additional broadening in z profile is likely due to the finite width of the tip.
concerns.summary: The claim that the edge-mode maximum lies in the monolayer is not supported, since tip broadening and the constant-height image (Fig. S7) place the enhanced signal in the bilayer.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.note: Authors ran STM constant-current simulations, revised the boundary position (new Fig. S6) and withdrew the statement on edge-mode location. v1 main text states the maximum is in the ML (Fig. 8c).

concerns.quote: I would suggest the authors to perform better analysis of their data, or focusing on areas where ML/BL Mn steps coincide with the Ta atomic step to better support their argument.
concerns.summary: Measure the edge mode at buried ML/BL boundaries that coincide with a Ta step to locate it unambiguously.
concerns.note: Authors argued such buried edges are not along high-symmetry directions and are impractical to study.

concerns.quote: They also proposed that similar spin-polarized edge states along the [11-0] (Zigzag) direction. Is such an edge state observed experimentally? A section of [11-0] edge is shown in Fig. 4b, but I do not see any signature
concerns.summary: The predicted direction dependence of the edge modes (present or absent along [1-10] for ML, BL and ML/BL edges) is not tested experimentally.
concerns.note: R2 point 5 asks the same for ML versus BL edges to Ta. Authors pointed to a weak example in Fig. S9b and said other [1-10] edges do not occur in their morphology.

concerns.quote: Are the spin-polarization of the edge states topological in nature, or just a biproduct of the AFM magnetic structure at the sample edge? What is the significance that the state is spin polarized?
concerns.summary: It is unclear whether the edge-mode spin polarization is topological or simply inherited from the antiferromagnetic edge structure.

concerns.quote: What is the evidence for topological nodal point superconductivity in Mn ML and BL grown on Ta (110) surface? The manuscript observes suppressed superconducting gaps with lifted zero-energy DOS
concerns.summary: Gap filling in the ML and BL does not demonstrate a topological nodal-point phase; direct experimental evidence is missing.
concerns.note: Authors conceded energy resolution is insufficient to see the V-shaped DOS and relied on prior theory and their own calculations.

concerns.quote: How to prove a topologically nontrivial origin of the observed edge modes experimentally? ... what independent experimental evidence confirms the nontrivial nature of the edge modes?
concerns.summary: There is no independent experimental evidence that the edge modes are topologically nontrivial; the case rests on modelling.
concerns.note: Authors added discussion but stated they cannot provide rigorous experimental evidence; R2 remained unconvinced in round 2.

concerns.quote: how do the authors ensure that the experimental system resides in the same parameter space as the calculations? Given the tunability of theoretical parameters
concerns.summary: Because the tight-binding parameters are tunable, the paper does not show that the real system sits in the modelled parameter regime.

concerns.quote: Could the observed edge modes arise from impurity states (Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states)? The step edges of Mn ML and BL ... are not very sharp and contain amounts of defects and disorders.
concerns.summary: The edge signal, its inhomogeneity, spin polarization and asymmetric subgap spectra could be trivial YSR states from disordered or exposed magnetic edge atoms.
concerns.note: R3 point 3: 'It looks like the trivial Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states stemming from the exposed magnetic atoms at the boundary.' Authors argued metallic bonding, in-gap states also in island interiors, and atomically straight edges; R2 still unsatisfied in round 2.

concerns.quote: It is well-known that trivial Andreev bound states can also arise between two superconductors even at zero phase difference. Can the author distinguish their observed states from the non-topological Andreev bound states
concerns.summary: The edge modes could be trivial Andreev bound states at the boundary between two superconductors.
concerns.note: Round 1: added an introduction paragraph and argued Andreev reflection needs perpendicular current flow; round 2 added an energy argument that strongly coupled ABS would sit near the coherence peaks.

concerns.quote: it seems likely that the spin-polarized signal is significantly stronger at the island edges than in the interior, and exhibits a strong contrast reverse between the up and down edges. What is the reason
concerns.summary: The stronger, reversed edge contrast in the spin-polarized current maps (Figs. 2b, 3a) is unexplained and may not fit the topological picture.
concerns.note: Authors explained it as a feedback-loop artifact of current maps at +5 mV and added this to captions and methods.

concerns.quote: this model seems to contradict their measurement because they show the properties of the normal Mn layers by an STM tip, not the properties of the superconducting Ta layers.
concerns.summary: Motivating the exchange coupling by induced moments in the Ta layer is inconsistent with measuring the Mn layer; the model's validity needs clarifying.

concerns.quote: But the subgap densities of states of the ML and the BL are highly asymmetric. ... Can the author explain the origin of such asymmetry
concerns.summary: The strong particle-hole asymmetry of the subgap spectra in Fig. 4c is unexplained.
concerns.note: Authors argued the spectral function, unlike the band structure, is asymmetric (Fig. 7b) and interior spectra show the same asymmetry.

concerns.quote: the actual experiment has no such periodicity and such assumption could cause the coupling between edge modes at different boundaries in their calculations.
concerns.summary: The periodic alternating-stripe geometry may couple edge modes across stripes and differs from the authors' earlier modelling.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.note: Authors added width convergence tests (new Fig. S21) and explained why the stripe geometry avoids trivial vacuum edges.

concerns.quote: It seems that there is something wrong with referencing Ref.[21]. There are question marks in the citings.
concerns.summary: Citations of Ref. 21 render as question marks.
concerns.note: In v1 Ref. 21 (Bruning et al.) and its citations render correctly, so this defect is not visible in v1.

later_concerns.quote: it remains essential to experimentally exclude other possibilities ... such as YSR states and Andreev bound states, as pointed out by not just one reviewer
later_concerns.summary: The revision adds discussion but still provides no experimental evidence excluding YSR and Andreev bound states.
later_concerns.note: Authors argued ABS would lie near the coherence peaks and so are excluded, conceded YSR cannot be completely ruled out, and slightly revised the ABS discussion. R2 recommended publication in round 3.

later_concerns.quote: the approach of combining experimental observations with theoretical simulations to confirm topologically nontrivial states has encountered numerous issues in the field of topological superconductivity.
later_concerns.summary: Agreement with simulations is not enough to establish topology; stronger confirmatory or exclusionary experimental evidence is needed.
later_concerns.note: No new data; authors defended reliance on tight-binding agreement.

first_round.quote: what I find missing is the novelty from the manuscript... As a result, I cannot recommend this paper to Nature Communication.

More rigorous experimental evidence, or exclusions of alternative possibilities (e.g., YSR states), are needed. Therefore, I cannot recommend the publication of this manuscript in Nature Communications.
This study may be worth publishing in Nat. Commun., however, it is not easy to make this determination... several questions and comments which should be properly answered before I can make a decision

recommendations.note: First round is Version 0 in this file; there is no sign of a transfer from another journal. No referee used the scale words, so all three recommendations are inferred. R1 and R2 are coded as reject because each says it 'cannot recommend' publication in Nature Communications: R1 on grounds of novelty, R2 because the topological origin is not established. R3 withheld a decision until substantive questions were answered, including distinguishing the observed states from Andreev bound states and YSR states, so R3 is coded as major revision. In later rounds R1 and R3 recommended publication in Version 1, and R2 recommended publication in Version 2.
recommendations.label: contested
